hint: To undo multiplying by a fraction, you can multiply by the fraction flipped over.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Read the equation as "two thirds of $x$ is $10$". If two of the three equal parts make $10$, how big is one part?
To undo multiplying by a fraction, you can multiply by the fraction flipped over.
Multiply both sides by $\frac{3}{2}$, the reciprocal of $\frac{2}{3}$. That leaves $x = 10 \times \frac{3}{2}$.
$10 \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{30}{2} = 15$, so the solution of the equation is $x = 15$.

explanation: The equation says that $\frac{2}{3}$ of the number $x$ equals $10$.
Multiply both sides by the reciprocal $\frac{3}{2}$, because $\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 1$ and that leaves $x$ alone.
The right side becomes $10 \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{30}{2}$, which simplifies to $15$.
Check: $\frac{2}{3} \times 15 = 10$ is true, so the solution is $x = 15$.
